title: Pieces of you
caption: You are not one self but a collage of selves, stitched together from every room you've ever stood in. This is an invitation to stop looking for the 'real' you and start collecting the fragments — the contradictions, the masks, the leftover pieces — and let them sit beside each other without apology.

title: The best of both worlds
caption: Wanting two things at once isn't indecision, it's honesty. Map out the tug-of-war between the lives you could lead, and notice how rarely you're asked to want just one thing.

title: The gaze you return
caption: Being looked at is not the same as being seen — and looking back is its own quiet rebellion. Trace what happens in your body the moment you stop absorbing a gaze and start meeting it.

title: Submission as strategy
caption: Sometimes bending is the smartest move in the room. Explore the difference between submitting because you have no choice and submitting because you're playing a longer game — and where that line gets blurry.

title: Accessing a future without limitations
caption: Fear is a brilliant editor; it cuts whole futures before you even get to read the draft. Write or draw the version of your life with that editor fired, just for one page.

title: This song made me think of…
caption: Some songs don't just soundtrack a moment, they hand you a mirror you didn't ask for. Follow one back to whoever — or whatever — it keeps reflecting.

title: The rules you inherited
caption: Long before you could question them, the rules were already moving in — about how to sit, want, speak, take up space. List the ones still running quietly in the background, and circle the ones you're ready to evict.

title: Summarise your day in third person
caption: Step outside of yourself for a moment and report back like a stranger watching from across the street. Distance has a way of revealing what proximity hides.

title: The Performer
caption: Everyone has a version of themselves built for an audience — the one who walks taller, laughs louder, edits in real time. Sketch that character, costume and all, and ask who they're performing for.

title: Heartbreak survival guide
caption: Write the manual nobody handed you: the rituals, the playlists, the small acts of defiance that get a person through. Make it practical, make it tender, make it yours.

title: Ask your family who you are
caption: Family holds an origin story about you that you've never fully read. Ask, collect the answers without correcting them, and place your own version next to theirs.

title: Make a protest sign about something ridiculous
caption: Protest doesn't have to be solemn to be sincere. Pick the smallest, silliest injustice you've ever felt and give it the full weight of a placard.

title: Guide to escaping creative paralysis
caption: The blank page is rarely about a lack of ideas; it's about the fear standing guard in front of them. Build yourself an exit route, step by step, for the next time you freeze.

title: What do you know?
caption: Not facts — instinct. Write down what you know in your body, the things you've never had to verify because they simply are.

title: Everything in your bag right now
caption: Empty it out. A bag is an unintentional self-portrait — the receipts, the half-used everything, the one item that doesn't belong but you can't throw away.

title: Revisit your 14 self
caption: She had opinions about who you'd become, and she was both right and completely wrong. Write her a letter, or better, let her write one to you.

title: What we carry together
caption: Some weight was never meant to be carried alone, even when we've been taught to act like it should be. Name what you're holding on behalf of someone else, and what it would mean to set part of it down, together.

title: Write down a recent argument
caption: Not to win it again — to look at it from a safe distance. Transcribe what was actually said, then what you wish had been said instead.

title: The version of you nobody has met yet
caption: She's been waiting in the wings this whole time, half-formed and unannounced. Describe her without rushing her into existence.

title: Describe your ideal government
caption: Forget what's realistic for a moment and design the world as it should run, not as it does. Who holds power, who doesn't, and why does it finally feel fair?

title: Take a picture of strangers holding hands
caption: Tenderness happens in public more than we notice, if we're paying attention. Go find proof of it and bring it back.

title: What's wrong with the people in my class?
caption: A tongue-in-cheek autopsy of the small, harmless ways we judge a room of strangers within seconds. Write the verdicts you'd never say out loud, then turn the mirror around.

title: What you would risk
caption: There's a version of bravery that has nothing to do with being fearless and everything to do with deciding something is worth the fall. Name what you'd actually be willing to lose, and for what.

title: Draw a scene from a film that changed you
caption: Some scenes lodge themselves somewhere permanent, rearranging how you see everything after. Draw it from memory, imperfect lines and all, and notice what your hand chooses to keep.

title: The silence that was passed down
caption: Some inheritances are absences — the things nobody said, the topics that closed a room. Give shape to the silence that's been handed down through your family, and decide whether you're going to keep it.

title: Outfit of the day
caption: Clothes are a daily decision about who you're choosing to be. Document today's choice and the small negotiation behind it.

title: The self you refuse to see
caption: There's a version of you that doesn't make it into the self-portrait, the one you edit out before anyone looks. Let her in, just this once, without flinching.

title: Ways to say "I Love You" without saying it
caption: Love rarely announces itself in those exact three words; it shows up sideways, in gestures and habits and the way someone remembers how you take your coffee. Catalogue the quieter dialects of affection you actually speak.

title: Draw the news
caption: Skip the headline and draw the feeling underneath it instead. Let today's news become an image instead of another scroll.

title: Photograph a scar
caption: A scar is proof the body survived something and kept going anyway. Photograph one — yours or someone else's, with permission — and let it be evidence, not apology.

title: Defeat your inner imposter
caption: That voice insisting you don't belong here has never once been right about anything. Write the rebuttal it's never gotten.

title: Describe the people you admire
caption: Admiration is a map of who we're quietly trying to become. List the people who hold something you want, and name exactly what that something is.

title: The last memory
caption: Some memories arrive knowing they're the last of their kind, even before you do. Write the one that's still holding its shape, and what it left behind.

title: Interview someone about becoming
caption: Ask someone older, or simply someone further along, how they became who they are. Let their answer complicate everything you assumed about arriving.

title: A day in objects
caption: Forget the narrative — just the objects. List everything you touched, moved, or carried today, and let the inventory tell its own quiet story.

title: We interrupt this programme
caption: Imagine you could break into the broadcast, just for thirty seconds, and say the thing nobody's saying. Write the interruption.

title: The body I inherited
caption: Long before it was yours to decide, your body arrived carrying someone else's hands, someone else's posture, someone else's history. Trace the parts of it that aren't fully your own invention.

title: The shape of wanting
caption: Desire rarely sits still long enough to be named cleanly. Give it a shape instead — a drawing, a diagram, a silhouette of what wanting actually feels like in you.

title: The room before you enter it
caption: There's a version of every room that exists in the seconds before you walk in — expectation, posture, the small performance of arrival. Describe that threshold moment, before the room gets to react to you.

title: The conversation you keep postponing
caption: You know the one. Write the version you'd say if you weren't waiting for the perfect moment that never actually comes.

title: Names I have worn
caption: Nicknames, titles, the names given in anger or in love — each one is a costume that fit for a while. List the names you've answered to, and what each one asked of you.

title: The authority you claim
caption: Nobody crowns you an expert on your own life; you have to take that authority for yourself. Write the territory only you get to have the final say over.

title: What song sounds every time you look at the one you love?
caption: Some people come with their own soundtrack, uninvited and impossible to mute. Name the song, and what it's actually trying to tell you.

title: What would your mother/father figure say?
caption: Their voice has a way of showing up in your head long after the conversation ended. Write what they'd say about where you are right now, and what you'd say back.

title: The story you add to the wall
caption: Every wall of stories needs one more confession, one more thing finally said out loud. Add yours, anonymous or not.

title: How to behave in a crowd
caption: We all carry an unwritten etiquette for disappearing safely into a group. Write the instructions you've absorbed without ever being taught them directly.

title: Intimacy without touch
caption: Closeness doesn't always need a hand to hold it together. Map the moments of intimacy that happened entirely without contact — eye contact, silence, the right word at the right time.

title: The work of being yourself
caption: Authenticity is sold as effortless, but it's labour, like everything else worth having. Document what it actually takes, on an ordinary day, to be recognisably you.

title: What you would burn down if you weren't so reasonable
caption: Reasonableness is its own quiet cage sometimes. Name what you'd let go up in flames if you stopped negotiating with yourself for one minute.

title: Send this page to someone who needs it
caption: Make this page for someone else's eyes instead of your own, for once. Who needs to see it, and what would you want them to find here?

title: Write a manifesto for something nobody defends
caption: Pick the unfashionable, the unglamorous, the thing everyone quietly mocks, and defend it with total conviction. Manifestos work best when nobody asked for them.

title: Dress code
caption: Every space has an unspoken dress code, written or not, and a cost for breaking it. Write the rules you've learned to read on sight, and where you've chosen to ignore them.

title: The unsent conversation
caption: Somewhere there's a message still sitting in drafts, a conversation that exists only in your head. Write it out in full, and decide, just for yourself, whether it needed an audience at all.

title: Five events that made you who you are
caption: Not the whole story — just the five hinge points where something turned. List them plainly, no need to explain or justify.

title: Advise your former self
caption: She couldn't have known then what you know now, and that's exactly the point. Write her the advice she wasn't ready to hear yet.

title: What would you say if they were actually listening?
caption: Most of us have rehearsed a version of honesty we never quite deliver. Say it here first, exactly as it would sound if you knew it would land.

title: Describe someone who made you feel seen
caption: Being truly seen is rare enough to remember exactly who did it and how. Describe that person, and the specific moment they made the invisible parts of you visible.
